## Combine and inspect tools (`pd-combine`, `pd-inspect`) {#sec-ch14-tools}

### Summary

Both are entry points of the `snapy` package (`[project.scripts]`,
{{< code pyproject.toml >}}).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Two command-line tools: `pd-combine` joins frames in time and merges streams; `pd-inspect` lists tensors.

**Data.** `pd-combine` reads combined `*.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc` frames; `pd-inspect` reads `.part` and `.restart` files.

**Placement.** After a run, from the shell; entry points of the `snapy` Python package.

**Activation.** Command line. `pd-combine` needs NCO[^rg-03439042d4b4]'s `ncrcat` and `ncks` on the `PATH`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Values are copied by NCO unchanged; blocks are not joined in space.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch14-tools-tests.
:::

Local symbols: none. This section uses no mathematical symbol.

### Derivation

There is no equation, and the tools copy values without arithmetic, so there is no round-off. Why `pd-combine` does
not join per-block files in space, in three steps (`ParseOutputFields`,
{{< code python/api/pd_combine.py ParseOutputFields >}}):

1. *The glob.* It collects `*.out*.<5 digits>.nc`, which matches per-block files `<basename>.block<r>.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc`
   as well as combined frames.
2. *The split.* It takes the last three dot-separated fields as stream, stamp and extension, and everything before
   them as the case. For a per-block file the case is `<basename>.block<r>`.
3. *Hence* each block is its own case, and `CombineTimeseries` concatenates that block's frames in time only.

### Numerical method

**`pd-combine <ids> [-d dir] [-o name] [--no-remove] [--no-merge]`.** `ParseOutputFields` globs
`*.out*.<5 digits>.nc` in the directory and splits each name into case, stream and stamp
(`ParseOutputFields`, {{< code python/api/pd_combine.py ParseOutputFields >}}). For each case and stream, `CombineTimeseries` runs
`ncrcat` over the stamps into `<case>.out<n>.nc`, or renames a single stamp. Unless `--no-remove`, it then deletes the
per-stamp files (`CombineTimeseries`, {{< code python/api/pd_combine.py CombineTimeseries >}}). Unless `--no-merge`, `CombineFields`
appends the listed streams into the first with `ncks -A` and moves the result to `<case>-<name>.nc`
(`CombineFields`, {{< code python/api/pd_combine.py CombineFields >}}). `main` checks that each requested id exists and also
calls `CombineFITS` for FITS outputs ({{< code python/api/pd_combine.py main >}}).

`pd-combine` does not join blocks in space. A per-block file `<basename>.block<r>.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc` (left by
`combine: false`) also matches the glob, with case `<basename>.block<r>`, so each block's frames are concatenated in
time on their own. Joining blocks is done by the run itself (@sec-ch14-netcdf).

**`pd-inspect <paths>`.** For each path, `inspect_path` checks for the bundle magic. For a bundle it prints the
tensors of every part (name, shape, dtype); otherwise it reads the file as one part
(`inspect_path`, {{< code python/api/pd_inspect.py inspect_path >}}).

### Code

**A minimal input.** The ids are the positions of the outputs in the deck's `outputs:` list, counting from 0. A
deck whose list is

```yaml
outputs:
  - type: restart          # id 0: writes card.<5 digits>.restart, no .nc frames
    dt: 300.
  - type: netcdf           # id 1: card.out1.<5 digits>.nc
    variables: [prim]
    dt: 300.
  - type: netcdf           # id 2: card.out2.<5 digits>.nc
    variables: [uov]
    dt: 300.
```

has NetCDF streams 1 and 2. `pd-combine` works on every case whose frames are in the directory it is given, and
it stops when one of them lacks a stream that another has. So run the example in a directory of its own, not in
`build/bin`, where the runs of [Install and run](#sec-preface-install) leave `straka_proc2.out0.*.nc`; there the
command stops with `ncrcat: ERROR file "./card.out0.?????.nc" not found`. From `build/bin`:

```bash
mkdir -p combine-demo && cd combine-demo
cp ../straka_proc2.yaml card.yaml      # then replace its outputs: list with the one above
torchrun --no-python --nproc-per-node=2 --master-port=29573 ../straka.release card.yaml   # any free port
pd-combine 1,2 -d . -o main --no-remove
pd-inspect card.00002.restart
```

`pd-combine` joins both streams in time and merges them into one file, `card-main.nc`, keeping the per-frame files;
`pd-inspect` lists the tensors of one restart file.

**What is refused, and why.** `pd-combine` exits with "Error: output id … not found!" when a requested stream has no
frame in the directory, before it touches any file (`main`, {{< code python/api/pd_combine.py main >}}). A missing
`ncrcat` or `ncks` makes the NCO call fail. `pd-inspect` reads a file without the bundle magic as one part.

**The excerpt.** Steps 1 and 2, in `ParseOutputFields`:

```python
files = glob(path + "/*.out*.[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9].nc")
for fname in files:
    field, stamp, ext = os.path.basename(fname).split(".")[-3:]
    case = ".".join(os.path.basename(fname).split(".")[:-3])
```

: Tests of the tools. {#tbl-ch14-tools-tests}

There is no check script: the section derives nothing.[^ch14-tools-run] No ctest tests either tool on its own. The `FULL_TESTS` decomposition runners call `pd-combine 0 -o main` on each
case: `run_shallow_splash_decomp.py` skips (exit 125) without it, and `run_shallow_xy_decomp.py` fails without it
(`pd_combine`, {{< code tests/run_shallow_xy_decomp.py main >}}). `pd-inspect` is used by no test.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `pd-combine` globs every matching `*.out*.nc` in the directory, leftovers included; run it in a clean directory.
- It needs NCO on the `PATH` and deletes its inputs by default.
- It does not join per-block files in space.
:::
